_help: Customer support lead at Lumen Cloud, gating send_email. Every threshold has a one-sentence 'why'.
on_ezio_failure_why: Fail closed: a wrong email to a customer cannot be unsent, so without Ezio's tone and fact-check signals a person reviews it; a fact our own price sheet proves wrong is still a BLOCK because that check never needs Ezio.
tier_decisions_why: GREEN only means 'no problem found', so it is approve-unless-our-checks-object; YELLOW is genuinely uncertain and worth a manager's minute; RED means Ezio found a concrete problem, so the email must not go out.

tone.why: Business rule 4 forbids hype even when the facts are right; normal support replies score 90+ while promotional ones fall well under 60, so 60 separates them with margin on both sides.

bias.why: A support email should not be one-sided or slanted; below 60 the mock marks framing as notably biased, which a manager should see before it reaches a customer.

agreement.why: Low agreement means the draft just echoes the customer (rule 4: don't agree with an incorrect claim); below 60 is sycophancy a manager should check.

when_accuracy_not_scored_why: Rule 5: Ezio can't see our prices, so most support emails come back not_scored; our own source-of-truth check covers those facts, and holding every not_scored email would block routine replies.
when_accuracy_unavailable_why: The fact-check service being down means public claims (laws, regulations) went unchecked, and our files can't cover them, so a person confirms before sending; facts our data proves wrong still BLOCK.
